summary: This is a plausible, rules-clean latency-hiding change to the single kernel on the sliding decode shapes (S=16, BLOCK_N=64, so 2 tiles per program, and this hoists half of them); judge it on the _sliding_fused_kernel profile row rather than the headline, because the expected ~1.5% headline gain sits inside the CI.
justification: The mechanism holds up. Every sliding decode shape spends 100% of its time in _sliding_fused_kernel (10.4us at decode_1 with only 32 CTAs, 12.9us at decode_16, 22.1us at decode_32). At decode_1 the floor is 0.1us, so the kernel is pure latency: a serial chain of dependent DRAM round trips under a cold L2. That chain is q load -> norm/rope -> seq load -> page-index load -> KV load, x2 tiles, then partial store -> ticket -> .cg reloads -> gate load. With count = 2047 and S = 16, chunk = 128 = 2 BLOCK_N tiles. Hoisting tile 0's seq->page->KV loads ahead of the q work removes about one round trip plus the norm/rope from the critical path. On a ~10us kernel that is roughly 0.5-1.5us (5-12%) at decode_1, consistent with the 'faster' call. The gain shrinks at decode_16/32, where 512/1024 CTAs over ~132 SMs make occupancy and bandwidth hide more latency; 'faster but smaller' is right there, and flat is equally likely. 'Flat' for full and verify is correct: kernel_fn routes only window && q_len == 1 here. Headline arithmetic: on the decode_1 load, the sliding shape is 46*13.2 = 607us vs full 16*27.3 = 437us. A 1us kernel gain is about 4.4% of that load and about 0.7% of the 6-load geomean, plus small decode_16/32 contributions, so the headline lands inside the +/-1.5% CI and the reported 2-3.5% decode_1 batch drift. Weakest link: the argument assumes the compiled code really does serialize as the source does. ptxas can already float the independent seq load above the q math. Triton's num_stages=2 pipeliner already issues the loop's first-iteration loads in a prologue, which today sits after the q and new-key work. If ptxas already overlaps part of the chain, the gain is smaller than estimated. Also, holding kb0/vb0 (2 x 64x64 fp8, ~16 regs/thread at 4 warps) live across _norm_rope and the S-1 new-key dot/stores adds register pressure. Spills would eat the gain; check the compiled kernel's n_spills/n_regs.
confounders: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: set S = 16 for every decode batch, which fixes tiles-per-program at 2. The hoisted tile's relative value depends directly on this (with fewer splits, more tiles per program, smaller relative gain), so the result is specific to S = 16 / BLOCK_N = 64. It is not a confound of attribution, though, since the split count is unchanged by this hypothesis.
sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: introduced _sliding_fused_kernel and its fixed source ordering (q work before seq/page loads), the very thing being changed. No interaction beyond being the base.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: does not touch the sliding path, but its run recorded a sliding decode_1 'loss' with no code change on that path. That is direct evidence of a 2-3.5% between-batch drift on exactly the shape this targets, so a headline-level sliding decode_1 move of that size is uninterpretable without the per-kernel row.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is a single mechanism (instruction ordering) on one kernel, with no landed hypothesis whose revert or retune would change its sign. The split count only scales its size. The real ambiguity is noise, not interference, and the in-run SGLang pairing plus the profile's _sliding_fused_kernel row (10.4 / 12.9 / 22.1us today) resolve it better than a second run would. A num_stages or tile-count retune would test a different hypothesis (and sliding-decode-blockn128-single-tile already covers the tile-count axis). Read a >= 0.5us drop on the decode_1 kernel row as a gain and an unchanged or higher row as a null, regardless of the headline.
open_questions: The change text says seq is 'already loaded from seq_ptr' at the top, but in master `seq = tl.load(seq_ptr + b)` comes after the q load/norm/rope. The implementer must move the seq load up as well (and compute n there), or the hoist only partly overlaps.

Does the compiled kernel spill once kb0/vb0 are live across _norm_rope and the S-1 new-key block? Compare n_regs/n_spills before and after; if it spills, reduce what stays live (for example, issue only the page and K loads early and V after the q work).

Should the hoist cover both tiles of the 128-key chunk, not just tile 0? Today tile 1's loads still wait behind tile 0's dot/softmax unless the pipeliner prefetches them. This overlaps sliding-decode-blockn128-single-tile; if that one wins, this is subsumed.
Scheduling note, not a defect: if sliding-cuda-cluster-dsmem-onelaunch (running) lands and replaces this kernel on every sliding shape at tp8/page 1, this becomes moot. Gate dispatch on that outcome.
